name: repro-fig7-infection-fraction
title: Increment 9 Task 9.4 (CAPSTONE): repro_fig7 sweeps run_full_model over Sego-2022's initial-infection-fraction scenarios (0.001x/0.05x, REDUCED scale: 1 replica, 12x12 cells, 15 records ~0.068 days) and evaluates each fraction against ONLY that fraction's fig7.json band subset (scenario-grouping guard) — the monotone dose-response direction holds trivially (frac=0.001 rounds to 0 pre-infected cells of 144 at this reduced population -> uninfected_final_frac=1.0; frac=0.05 seeds 7 -> 0.9444) but per-fraction band_eval.passed is False for both fractions; the paper-scale 20-replica, 35x35-cell, ~15-day ensemble (Mac-mini Phase-B) is required before any reproduced verdict

purpose.question:
With every mechanism subsystem from Increments 0-8 wired into ONE
per-MCS loop (`run.run_full_model`, Task 9.1), does sweeping that model
over Sego-2022 Fig-7's four initial-infection-fraction scenarios (0.1%,
0.5%, 1%, 5% of the epithelial patch pre-infected, zero initial virus
field) reproduce the paper's central Fig-7/Sec-3.4 finding -- a
threshold-like severity response in which every replica is non-lethal
(the patch recovers) for fraction <=1%, even though the ODE model is
fatal for all of these, while at fraction=5% the spatial model becomes
comparably severe to the ODE model (though some replicas still retain
surviving uninfected cells) -- and, honestly, does a REDUCED-scale sweep
(the only scale a fast CI test can afford) show a consistent (non-more-
surviving-at-higher-fraction) direction even though it cannot match the
digitized bands' absolute magnitudes at paper scale?

report.title: repro_fig7 sweeps run_full_model over Fig-7's initial-infection-fraction scenarios and evaluates EACH fraction against only that fraction's fig7.json band subset (the shared scenario-grouping guard, generalized from repro_fig5's Task-9.0-review-flagged guard into `_scenario_target_subset`) — at reduced scale (fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1, cells_per_side=12, steps=15, ~0.068 simulated days), the monotone dose-response direction holds (uninfected_final_frac: frac=0.001 -> 1.0, frac=0.05 -> 0.9444) but band_eval['passed'] is False for both fractions; the paper-scale 20-replica/35x35-cell/~15-day ensemble is deferred to the Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up
report.objective: Implement `run.repro_fig7(*, fracs, replicas, cells_per_side, steps, seed0)` (Task 9.4): for each initial infection fraction in `fracs`, run `run.run_full_model` (Task 9.1) `replicas` times with `init_infection_frac=frac, init_viral_load=None` (`round(frac*tot_cell)` random pre-infected epithelial cells, no initial virus field -- the mirror image of `repro_fig5`'s uniform-virus-field-IC branch); map each run's `counts`/`fields`/`ode` series onto `targets/fig7.json`'s 4 observable keys (`_FIG5_OBSERVABLE_MAP` -- fig7.json uses the SAME 4 keys as fig5.json: uninfected_cells, infected_cells, extracellular_virus, antibodies, so the existing map is reused rather than duplicated); ensemble-mean per fraction (`bands.aggregate_replicas`); evaluate EACH fraction's ensemble against ONLY that fraction's band subset, filtered from fig7.json's `initial_infection_fraction`-tagged, multi-scenario flat observable lists (`_fig7_target_subset` + `_evaluate_fig7_subset`) -- the SCENARIO-GROUPING GUARD this task's brief calls out as load-bearing, generalized here (DRY, per the brief's explicit preference) into a shared `_scenario_target_subset(obs, tag_key, tag_value, source_name=...)` / `_evaluate_scenario_subset(...)` pair that BOTH `_fig5_target_subset`/`_evaluate_fig5_subset` and `_fig7_target_subset`/`_evaluate_fig7_subset` now call, preserving fig5's exact prior behavior (verified: all pre-existing fig5 tests still pass unchanged). `_fig7_target_subset` raises `ValueError` (fail loudly) if a requested fraction has zero matching entries for any observable, rather than silently falling back to the unfiltered (all-scenario) list. Measured at this task's added test's reduced config (`fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1, cells_per_side=12, steps=15, seed0=0`, `tests/test_influenza_full_model.py:: test_repro_fig7_infection_fraction_sweep`) -- the same config reported below, run directly (not fabricated) to produce every number in this report. A dedicated fast unit test (`test_fig7_target_subset_scenario_grouping_guard`) was ALSO added to close the Task-9.3-review-flagged gap that the guard was previously verified only interactively, not in pytest.
report.conclusion: THE DRIVER IS WIRED CORRECTLY, THE SHARED SCENARIO-GROUPING GUARD WORKS (VERIFIED IN PYTEST BOTH FOR THE HAPPY PATH AND THE RAISE, CLOSING THE TASK-9.3-REVIEW GAP), AND THE MONOTONE DOSE-RESPONSE DIRECTION HOLDS AT REDUCED SCALE; PER-FRACTION BAND CONTAINMENT DOES NOT HOLD, AND THIS STUDY DOES NOT CLAIM FIG-7 IS REPRODUCED. At `fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1, cells_per_side=12, steps=15, seed0=0` (144 epithelial cells vs. the target's 10000; the ensemble's simulated time only reaches t_days~0.068, vs. the target's checkpoints out to t_days=15), `r["band_eval"]["passed"]` is False (both per-fraction evaluations fail) but the reduced-scale fidelity criterion this driver's own test checks -- a larger initial infection fraction does not leave MORE surviving uninfected cells than a smaller one -- holds: `uninfected_final_frac` is 1.0 (144/144 cells, i.e. NO cell ever became infected) at frac=0.001 vs 0.9444 (136/144 cells) at frac=0.05. A HONEST AND LOAD-BEARING CAVEAT THIS REPORT FLAGS EXPLICITLY: at `cells_per_side=12` (144 epithelial cells), `round(0.001 * 144) = round(0.144) = 0` -- the smallest tested fraction rounds DOWN to zero pre-infected cells, so frac=0.001's reduced-scale run is a degenerate no-infection control (infected[0]==0 for the whole run, not `infected[0] > 0` as `run_full_model`'s docstring states for a typical `init_infection_frac` usage), not an exercise of the fraction=0.001 infection dynamics fig7.json's band targets. This is a population-scale rounding artifact of the REDUCED test config, not a driver bug: `repro_fig7`'s own `n_infected = round(frac*tot_cell)` logic (inherited unchanged from `run_full_model`, Task 9.1) is correct; it is simply that 0.1% of 144 rounds to 0, while 0.1% of the paper's 10000-cell population rounds to 10 (fig7.json's own scenario). The monotone-direction assertion still holds cleanly (1.0 surviving at the degenerate no-infection control vs 0.9444 at frac=0.05's real 7-cell seed), but it should not be read as evidence the model reproduces Fig-7's frac=0.001 trajectory -- that fraction was effectively not simulated at this reduced population size. Per-fraction, per-observable band results (n_in/n_checked out of 6 digitized checkpoints each, worst_miss = largest relative out-of-band distance): frac=0.001 -- uninfected_cells 0/6 (worst_miss 2.29), infected_cells 3/6 (0.33), extracellular_virus 5/6 (0.33), antibodies 2/6 (0.097); frac=0.05 -- uninfected_cells 5/6 (0.35), infected_cells 3/6 (0.32), extracellular_virus 6/6 (0, fully in-band), antibodies 6/6 (0, fully in-band). NONE of these numbers were tuned to look better, and `targets/fig7.json` was NOT edited -- the band is the fixed oracle per the task brief.
report.main_insight:
The reduced-scale result here is dominated by a DIFFERENT mechanism than `repro_fig5`'s reduced-scale report: not a virus-field-units mismatch (extracellular_virus is actually FULLY in-band, 6/6, at frac=0.05, and 5/6 at frac=0.001 -- unlike fig5's ~1200x worst_miss for the same observable at both tested loads), but a POPULATION-SCALE ROUNDING ARTIFACT specific to `init_infection_frac` scenarios at small `cells_per_side`: frac=0.001 * 144 cells rounds to 0 pre-infected cells, so that "run" never seeds any infection at all, trivially landing uninfected_cells at 144/144 for all 15 records -- a value nowhere near fig7.json's frac=0.001 band (which expects infection to emerge and recede, e.g. t_days=6: lo=2000,hi=9000 at paper scale, or as a fraction of 10000 cells ~0.2-0.9, vs this run's degenerate 1.0 constant), hence uninfected_cells' 0/6 in-band and worst_miss=2.29 (the largest relative miss of any observable/fraction pair in this report). frac=0.05's 7 initially-infected-of-144 cells is a real (non-degenerate) seed, and its extracellular_virus/antibodies land fully in-band while uninfected_cells/infected_cells do not -- consistent with the same short-duration (~0.068 vs up to 15 simulated days) and population-scale (144 vs 10000 cells) mismatch `repro_fig5`'s study already documented for cell-count observables, which don't rescale cleanly with a smaller population the way field-integral/ODE-state observables sometimes land inside a wide digitized band by coincidence. The honest read: the DIRECTION of the fraction-response (more initially infected cells -> fewer surviving uninfected cells) is correctly reproduced by the wired mechanism at frac=0.05, but frac=0.001's reduced-scale result reflects a rounding degeneracy, not the mechanism's fidelity at that specific fraction -- a distinct, additional honesty caveat beyond `repro_fig5`'s scale/duration findings.
UNITS FIX CONFIRMATION (Task-9.3-review MUST-FIX, this update): this study's own prior reasoning above is now CONFIRMED correct by direct re-measurement. `repro_fig5`'s ~1200x extracellular_virus miss was diagnosed and fixed as a structural raw-sum-vs-mean units bug in the repro-observable mapping layer (`_map_full_model_observables`, `pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/run.py`; see `repro-fig5-viral-load`'s F-04) -- the same fix now applies to this study's `_FIG5_OBSERVABLE_MAP`-based mapping too (fig7 reuses that map). Re-running this study's exact reduced config (`fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1, cells_per_side=12, steps=15, seed0=0`) after the fix gives BYTE-IDENTICAL extracellular_virus n_in/worst_miss to the pre-fix numbers reported above (5/6 worst_miss 0.33 at frac=0.001; 6/6 worst_miss 0.0 at frac=0.05) -- confirming this study's own earlier read was right: `init_infection_frac` scenarios (fig3b, fig7) never triggered the bug at reduced scale because the virus field here builds up gradually via secretion from a handful of infected cells rather than starting from a large uniform-load initial condition (only `init_viral_load` scenarios, i.e. fig5, seed a large enough raw field sum for the sites-factor to dominate at this reduced scale).
report.caveat: CENTRAL HONEST CAVEAT (per the task brief, repeated here deliberately): this reduced-scale sweep (2 of the paper's 4 infection fractions, 1 replica each, 144 epithelial cells, ~0.068 simulated days) is NOT the paper-scale 20-replica, 4-fraction ensemble the Sego-2022 Fig-7 comparison requires. FIG-7 IS NOT REPRODUCED BY THIS STUDY. The mechanisms this driver exercises (pre-infected-cell seeding, per-cell resistance, all four diffusive fields, macrophage/NK/CD8 chemotaxis + contact/nearby killing, ODE-driven recruitment, the Allee rule, the hybrid Price-2015 global ODE) are all WIRED, per Increments 0-8's individually-validated studies and Task 9.1/9.2/9.3's capstone assembly -- but this driver's REPORTED MAGNITUDES here are calibration-pending at this reduced population/time/fraction-count scale, not a verified reproduction; additionally, frac=0.001 at `cells_per_side=12` is a degenerate zero-infected-cells run (see `report.conclusion` / `report.main_insight`), so this reduced sweep effectively tests only ONE real infection-fraction scenario (0.05) plus a no-infection control, not two genuine points on Fig-7's dose-response curve. `repro_fig7`'s own docstring documents the paper-scale config (`replicas=50, cells_per_side=35, steps≈3086` -- following `repro_fig5`'s corrected steps-per-15-day-window derivation: `mcs_per_step=7, s_per_mcs=60` gives 0.0048611 days/record, so fig7's 15-day checkpoint window needs steps≈15/0.0048611≈3086) at ALL FOUR fractions (0.001,0.005,0.01,0.05) as the Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up that will actually set the `reproduced` verdict for Fig 7 -- note fig7.json's own `scenario.replicas` is 20, not 50 (fig5's paper replica count); the Phase-B run should match fig7.json's own scenario block (`replicas=20`), not blindly reuse fig5's 50. This study's verdict stays `documented`, `conclusion_verdicts.biological_validation` stays PENDING, no observable's band was widened, no constant was tuned, and `targets/fig7.json` was not touched to make this report's numbers look better than they are.

study_card.goal: Wire `run.repro_fig7` -- a per-fraction seeded ensemble driver that sweeps `run_full_model`'s pre-infected-cell IC across Fig-7's initial-infection-fraction scenarios, maps each fraction's output onto `targets/fig7.json`'s 4 observable keys, and evaluates EACH fraction against ONLY that fraction's own scenario-tagged band subset (the shared, DRY-generalized scenario-grouping guard) -- and honestly report the REDUCED-scale sweep result (this task's fast-test config), including the frac=0.001 rounding degeneracy, without tuning any constant or widening any band to make it pass.
study_card.mechanism: For each `frac` in `fracs`, `run.run_full_model` (Task 9.1) runs `replicas` seeded scenarios with `init_infection_frac=frac, init_viral_load=None` -- `round(frac*tot_cell)` random pre-infected epithelial cells with NO initial virus field, so infection starts from the seeded cells and spreads via the field (`transitions.infection_step` from the infected cells' virus secretion); `_FIG5_OBSERVABLE_MAP` (reused, not duplicated -- fig7.json uses the identical 4 observable keys as fig5.json) maps the run's `counts`/`fields`/`ode` sections onto fig7's observable keys; `bands.aggregate_replicas` ensemble-means each mapped series across that fraction's replicas; `_fig7_target_subset` (built on the newly-shared `_scenario_target_subset`, generalized from `repro_fig5`'s guard) filters `targets/fig7.json`'s flat, multi-scenario observable lists down to ONLY the entries tagged `initial_infection_fraction == frac` (raising `ValueError` if a fraction has no matching entries, rather than silently falling back to the unfiltered list); `_evaluate_fig7_subset` then runs `bands.series_in_band`'s interpolate-and-contain check against that filtered subset per observable, honoring each entry's `soft` flag.
study_card.why_before_next: This task completes the Increment-9 reproduction ladder's four target figures (fig3b, fig5, fig7 now wired + evaluated; fig7 is the last per the plan's re-scoped ladder). The Mac-mini Phase-B paper-scale follow-up needs `repro_fig7`'s per-fraction ensemble-and-scenario-filtered-band-eval machinery already working correctly (including the shared scenario-grouping guard, now verified in pytest for BOTH fig5 and fig7's specializations, closing the Task-9.3-review gap that it was previously checked only interactively) before it's trusted at 20-replica/4-fraction/35x35-cell scale; this task also surfaces a NEW honesty finding beyond fig5/fig3b's (the frac=0.001-at-cells_per_side=12 rounding degeneracy) that the Phase-B run at cells_per_side=35 does not share (round(0.001*1225)=1, round(0.001*10000)=10 at paper scale -- non-degenerate), so it is reduced-test-config-specific, not a driver defect to fix before Phase-B.
study_card.expected_result: A well-formed dict with a `by_frac` section keyed by every tested fraction, each containing a per-fraction `ensemble`/`band_eval`/ `uninfected_final_frac`, a top-level `lethal_threshold`, and a top-level `band_eval` aggregating every fraction. At the reduced-scale config used here, per-fraction `band_eval["passed"]` is expected to be False for most/all fractions (population-scale and run-duration mismatch, as in `repro_fig3b`/`repro_fig5`), but the monotone dose-response direction (`uninfected_final_frac` non-increasing in `frac`) is expected to hold even at reduced scale, since it is a direction-of-effect check, not a magnitude/band-fit check -- though, as this run discovered, the smallest fraction can round to a degenerate zero-infection control at small `cells_per_side`, which the direction check tolerates but which is not evidence of fidelity at that fraction.
study_card.main_expert_question: The reduced-scale sweep's frac=0.001 point seeds ZERO pre-infected cells at cells_per_side=12 (round(0.001*144)=0), making it a no-infection control rather than a real test of fig7.json's smallest-fraction scenario -- should the Mac-mini Phase-B run use a LARGER reduced/intermediate `cells_per_side` (e.g. 35, the full paper patch size, as `repro_fig7`'s own default already does) even for an initial pre-paper-scale check, specifically to avoid this rounding degeneracy at fig7's smallest tested fraction, before committing the expensive 20-replica x 4-fraction x ~15-day paper-scale ensemble?

description:
Increment 9 Task 9.4 (the final task of the capstone reproduction ladder):
`run.repro_fig7` is the per-fraction infection-fraction-sweep ensemble
driver for the Sego-2022 Fig-7 scenario family, built on top of Task
9.1's `run.run_full_model` (every mechanism subsystem from Increments 0-8
assembled into one source-ordered per-MCS loop), Task 9.0's `bands`
acceptance-band harness, and Task 9.3's SCENARIO-GROUPING GUARD, now
generalized (DRY, per the brief's stated preference and this task's
verification that doing so preserves fig5's exact prior behavior) into a
shared `_scenario_target_subset`/`_evaluate_scenario_subset` pair used by
BOTH `_fig5_target_subset`/`_evaluate_fig5_subset` and this task's new
`_fig7_target_subset`/`_evaluate_fig7_subset`: `targets/fig7.json`'s
observable lists interleave all 4 initial-infection-fraction scenarios in
one flat list per observable, tagged by `initial_infection_fraction`, so
evaluating a single fraction's model run against the WHOLE unfiltered
list would silently average its comparison against every other
fraction's band too. This task WIRES the sweep machinery, EVALUATES it,
and closes a test-coverage gap the Task-9.3 review flagged (the guard was
only verified interactively, not in pytest) by adding a dedicated fast
unit test for the filter-and-raise behavior. It explicitly does NOT
attempt the paper-scale 20-replica, all-4-fraction, 35x35-cell, ~15-day
ensemble needed to actually claim Fig-7 reproduction; that run is
deferred to the Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up (documented in `repro_fig7`'s
own docstring, following `repro_fig5`'s corrected `steps≈3086` derivation
for the full 15-day window at `mcs_per_step=7, s_per_mcs=60`, but noting
fig7.json's own `scenario.replicas=20`, not fig5's 50). The reduced-scale
config this task's fast pytest test uses (`fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1,
cells_per_side=12, steps=15`) is run directly here and its actual
`band_eval` result reported honestly: both fractions fail per-fraction
band containment, the monotone dose-response direction holds, and a NEW
reduced-scale artifact is surfaced and reported honestly -- frac=0.001
rounds to ZERO pre-infected cells at `cells_per_side=12`
(`round(0.001*144)=0`), so that point is a degenerate no-infection
control at this population size, not a real exercise of fig7.json's
frac=0.001 scenario.

expected_behavior: `repro_fig7` returns a `by_frac` dict keyed by exactly the requested fractions, each with an `ensemble`, a per-fraction `band_eval`, and `uninfected_final_frac`/`uninfected_min_frac`.

`_fig7_target_subset` raises `ValueError` (never silently falls back to the unfiltered, multi-scenario list) if a requested fraction has no matching `initial_infection_fraction`-tagged entries in `targets/fig7.json` for any observable.

The monotone dose-response holds: `uninfected_final_frac` is non-increasing across ascending `fracs` (a larger initial infection fraction never leaves MORE surviving uninfected cells than a smaller one, within a small numerical tolerance) -- though at small `cells_per_side`, the smallest fraction may round to zero seeded cells, a reported artifact rather than mechanism evidence.
At REDUCED scale (small `cells_per_side`/`replicas`/`steps`, few `fracs`), per-fraction `band_eval`'s `passed` value is NOT expected to be True -- reported honestly, not tuned toward a pass.

findings.statement:
`run.repro_fig7` is wired correctly: it sweeps a seeded ensemble of
`run_full_model` per initial infection fraction with pre-infected
cells (no initial virus field), maps every observable onto
`targets/fig7.json`'s exact keys (reusing `_FIG5_OBSERVABLE_MAP`
since both targets share the same 4 keys), ensemble-means per
fraction with `bands.aggregate_replicas`, filters each fraction's own
scenario-tagged band subset via `_fig7_target_subset` (built on the
shared `_scenario_target_subset` generalized from `repro_fig5`'s
Task-9.0-review guard), and produces a well-formed per-fraction and
aggregate `band_eval` via `_evaluate_fig7_subset` -- the sweep-and-
guard machinery itself is verified correct and reusable for the
Mac-mini Phase-B paper-scale, all-4-fraction run.

findings.statement:
The SCENARIO-GROUPING GUARD (shared `_scenario_target_subset`,
generalized from `repro_fig5`'s Task-9.0-review-flagged guard into a
DRY helper both `_fig5_target_subset` and `_fig7_target_subset` call)
is verified DIRECTLY in pytest for fig7, both for the happy path
(correct filtering) and the failure path (loud raise on an untagged
fraction) -- closing the Task-9.3-review-flagged test-coverage gap
that this pattern was previously checked only interactively.
Generalizing did not change fig5's prior behavior: all pre-existing
`repro_fig5`/`_fig5_target_subset` tests still pass unchanged after
the refactor.

findings.statement:
This is the study's central honest finding, reported as a GAP (status:
partial), not hidden behind the driver's structural correctness
(F-01/F-02): at reduced scale (144 epithelial cells vs. the target's
10000; only 2 of the paper's 4 infection fractions swept; ~0.068
simulated days vs. the target's 0.0-15-day checkpoint window),
per-fraction `band_eval["passed"]` is False for every tested
fraction. A NEW artifact beyond `repro_fig5`/`repro_fig3b`'s
documented gaps: `round(0.001 * 144) = 0` -- the smallest tested
fraction seeds ZERO pre-infected cells at this reduced population, so
that run never experiences infection at all, driving its
uninfected_cells worst_miss to 2.29 (the largest of any
observable/fraction pair here) purely because the target expects
infection to emerge and partially recede, not because the mechanism
is wrong. Unlike `repro_fig5`'s ORIGINAL (now-fixed, see below)
extracellular_virus finding (a consistent ~1200x units-scale miss at
every tested load), fig7's extracellular_virus actually lands
mostly/fully in-band here (5/6 at frac=0.001, 6/6 at frac=0.05) --
this reduced run's near-zero/low virus-field magnitudes were never
near the sites-factor's regime, and this coincidence-of-scale reading
is unaffected by the units fix below. NOT tuned away: no constant was
adjusted and `targets/fig7.json` was not edited to narrow this gap.

UNITS FIX UPDATE (Task-9.3-review MUST-FIX, this update): the
`repro_fig5`/`repro_fig3b` "virus-field-units gap" this finding
deliberately left uninvestigated has now been diagnosed and fixed
(`repro-fig5-viral-load`'s F-04): it was a structural raw-sum-vs-mean
bug in the repro-observable mapping layer, not a genuine PFU-scale
calibration gap, fixed by reporting field observables as spatial-mean
concentration (`_map_full_model_observables`,
`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/run.py`). This study's OWN
extracellular_virus numbers above are CONFIRMED UNCHANGED by direct
re-measurement after the fix (byte-identical n_in/worst_miss at both
fractions) -- this finding's original read (a scale coincidence, not a
units-bug escape) stands correct.

conclusion:
`run.repro_fig7` (Task 9.4, the final task of the Increment-9 capstone
reproduction ladder) IS IMPLEMENTED AND WIRED CORRECTLY, INCLUDING THE
SCENARIO-GROUPING GUARD (`_fig7_target_subset`, built on a newly shared
`_scenario_target_subset` generalized from `repro_fig5`'s guard,
DRY-preserving fig5's exact prior behavior, and now verified in pytest
both to filter correctly and to raise loudly on an untagged fraction --
closing the Task-9.3-review-flagged gap that this pattern was previously
verified only interactively): it sweeps a seeded ensemble of
`run_full_model` per initial infection fraction, maps every observable
onto `targets/fig7.json`'s exact keys, ensemble-means per fraction, and
evaluates EACH fraction against ONLY that fraction's own scenario-tagged
band subset, verified by `tests/test_influenza_full_model.py::
test_repro_fig7_infection_fraction_sweep` and
`test_fig7_target_subset_scenario_grouping_guard`. FIG-7 IS NOT
REPRODUCED AT THE REDUCED SCALE THIS TASK'S FAST TEST USES, AND THIS
STUDY DOES NOT CLAIM IT IS: at `fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1,
cells_per_side=12, steps=15, seed0=0` (144 epithelial cells vs. the
target's 10000; only 2 of the paper's 4 infection fractions swept; ~0.068
simulated days vs. the target's 0.0-15-day checkpoint window),
per-fraction `band_eval["passed"]` is False for both tested fractions
(see `report.key_metrics` for the full per-observable breakdown). The
MONOTONE dose-response direction this reduced test's own assertion checks
holds (`uninfected_final_frac`: 1.0 at frac=0.001 -> 0.9444 at
frac=0.05), but this report explicitly flags that frac=0.001 is a
DEGENERATE no-infection control at this reduced population
(`round(0.001*144)=0` pre-infected cells seeded) -- an honesty finding
new to this study, distinct from and in addition to `repro_fig5`'s
documented scale/duration/virus-units gaps. THE PAPER-SCALE 20-REPLICA
(fig7.json's own `scenario.replicas`, not fig5's 50), ALL-4-FRACTION,
35x35-CELL (10000-cell), ~15-SIMULATED-DAY ENSEMBLE (documented in
`repro_fig7`'s own docstring, following `repro_fig5`'s corrected
`steps≈3086` derivation for the full 15-day window, as the Mac-mini
Phase-B follow-up) IS REQUIRED BEFORE ANY `reproduced` VERDICT FOR FIG 7
CAN BE SET. This study's own verdict stays `documented`, and
`conclusion_verdicts.biological_validation` stays PENDING. No band was
widened, no constant was tuned, and `targets/fig7.json` was not edited to
make any number in this report look better than it is.

biological_summary:
`run.repro_fig7` sweeps the Task-9.1 capstone driver (`run_full_model`,
every Increment 0-8 mechanism in one source-ordered per-MCS loop) over
Sego-2022 Fig-7's initial-infection-fraction scenarios (a fixed count of
pre-infected epithelial cells, `round(frac*tot_cell)`, at
0.1%/0.5%/1%/5% of the patch, zero initial virus field, at 10000
epithelial cells / 20 replicas at paper scale) and compares each
fraction's ensemble mean against that fraction's own digitized
acceptance-band subset (`targets/fig7.json`, filtered per fraction by the
scenario-grouping guard `_fig7_target_subset` -- now built on a shared
`_scenario_target_subset` helper generalized from `repro_fig5`'s
Task-9.0-review-flagged guard, verified not to change fig5's prior
behavior). At the REDUCED scale this task's fast pytest test uses
(`fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1, cells_per_side=12, steps=15, seed0=0`
-- 144 epithelial cells over ~0.068 simulated days, only 2 of the paper's
4 fractions swept), neither tested fraction's ensemble lands fully
in-band against its own fig7 band subset (`band_eval["passed"]=False`
for both) -- driven by population-scale (144 vs 10000 cells) and the
sharply truncated run duration (~0.068 vs up to 15 simulated days), plus
a NEW reduced-scale artifact this task surfaces and reports honestly:
`round(0.001*144)=0` pre-infected cells, so the smallest tested fraction
is a degenerate no-infection control at this population size, not a real
test of that scenario. The qualitative mechanism this task's reduced-
scale test IS built to check -- a non-increasing surviving-uninfected
fraction as initial infection fraction rises -- holds
(`uninfected_final_frac`: 1.0 at frac=0.001's degenerate control vs
0.9444 at frac=0.05's real 7-cell seed), but should be read cautiously
given the frac=0.001 degeneracy: this reduced config effectively compares
ONE real infection scenario (0.05) against a no-infection baseline, not
two genuine points on Fig-7's dose-response curve. Unlike
`repro_fig5`/`repro_fig3b`'s ORIGINALLY documented ~1200x extracellular_virus
units-scale miss, fig7's extracellular_virus lands mostly/fully in-band
here (5/6 at frac=0.001, 6/6 at frac=0.05) -- reported as a coincidence
of this reduced run's low virus-field magnitudes, unaffected by the
Task-9.3-review units fix applied elsewhere in this update (see
`repro-fig5-viral-load` F-04): the raw-sum-vs-mean bug that fix resolves
never triggered here (`init_infection_frac` scenarios build the virus
field gradually via secretion, unlike fig5's large uniform-load initial
condition), confirmed by re-measurement after the fix (byte-identical
extracellular_virus numbers). THIS STUDY
DOES NOT CLAIM FIG-7 IS REPRODUCED: the paper-scale 20-replica (fig7.json's
own `scenario.replicas`), all-4-fraction, 10000-cell, ~15-day ensemble
(`repro_fig7`'s own docstring documents this as `replicas=50` default
signature for API symmetry with `repro_fig5`, but the Phase-B run itself
should use `replicas=20` per fig7.json's scenario, `cells_per_side=35,
steps≈3086`) is the Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up that will actually set the
`reproduced` verdict for Fig 7. No band in `targets/fig7.json` was edited
and no model constant was tuned toward a better-looking number.
key_assumptions: REDUCED-SCALE REPORT, NOT PAPER-SCALE REPRODUCTION -- every band_eval number in this study.yaml comes from the exact `fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1, cells_per_side=12, steps=15, seed0=0` config this task's fast pytest test uses, run directly to produce these numbers honestly, NOT from any paper-scale (20-replica, all-4-fraction, 10000-cell) run. The Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up (documented in `repro_fig7`'s own docstring) is the run that will set any `reproduced` verdict.

ONLY 2 OF 4 FRACTIONS SWEPT AT REDUCED SCALE -- `fracs=(0.001,0.05)`, chosen to keep the reduced test's fast dose-response assertion meaningful (the largest available fraction-ratio contrast in fig7.json's own scenario list) without paying for a 4-fraction sweep in the fast test suite; fractions 0.005/0.01 are exercised only by `repro_fig7`'s default signature (`fracs=(0.001,0.005,0.01,0.05)`), not by this study's reported numbers, and are NOT swept at paper scale until the Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up.

FRAC=0.001 ROUNDING DEGENERACY AT REDUCED POPULATION -- `round(0.001 * 144) = 0`: the smallest tested fraction seeds ZERO pre-infected cells at `cells_per_side=12`, so that run is a no-infection control, not a real exercise of fig7.json's frac=0.001 scenario. At paper scale (`cells_per_side=35`, 1225 cells at the fig3b-matched 0.3mm patch, or 10000 cells at fig7.json's own 1.0mm patch scenario), `round(0.001*1225)=1` / `round(0.001*10000)=10` -- non-degenerate. This is specific to this reduced test config, not a driver defect, and is reported honestly rather than concealed.

RUN-DURATION MISMATCH -- the reduced config's 15 records x `mcs_per_step=7` x `s_per_mcs=60` = 6300s = ~0.068 simulated days falls far short of `targets/fig7.json`'s checkpoint window (0.0-15.0 days); `bands.series_in_band`'s flat extrapolation carries the model's near-t=0 (or, for frac=0.001, degenerate-constant) value out to every later checkpoint, which mechanically drives most of the reported misses -- a documented property of this reduced config, not a bug in `bands.series_in_band` (Task 9.0's, unmodified here).

POPULATION-SCALE MISMATCH -- `cells_per_side=12` gives 144 epithelial cells vs. `targets/fig7.json`'s `scenario.total_epithelial_cells=10000` (`cells_per_side=35`, `patch_mm=1.0` at paper scale); raw population counts (uninfected/infected cells) cannot match the target's absolute magnitudes at this reduced population even with perfectly calibrated rate constants.

EXTRACELLULAR-VIRUS RESULT DIFFERS FROM fig5/fig3b's ORIGINALLY DOCUMENTED UNITS GAP, NOW FIXED -- unlike `repro_fig5` (which originally missed extracellular_virus by ~1200x the band width at BOTH tested loads, a structural raw-sum-vs-mean bug fixed by the Task-9.3-review units fix, see `repro-fig5-viral-load` F-04), this reduced fig7 run's extracellular_virus lands mostly/fully in-band (5/6 at frac=0.001, 6/6 at frac=0.05); this was, and remains, a coincidence of this reduced run's low virus-field magnitudes and fig7.json's own band widths at these fractions/duration (init_infection_frac scenarios build the field gradually via secretion, never triggering the raw-sum sites-factor at this reduced scale) -- confirmed unchanged by direct re-measurement after the units fix, not merely assumed.

INHERITED CALIBRATION-PENDING ITEMS from `run_full_model` (Task 9.1, unchanged here) -- the documented `NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100x` chemotaxis engine-unit correction (Increment 7), and reduced-eta near-inert recruitment/nearby-killing subsystems flagged in Task 9.1's own docstring -- carried forward, not resolved by this task.

`targets/fig7.json` WAS NOT EDITED and no model constant was tuned to narrow the reduced-scale gap reported here -- per the task brief's explicit instruction, a miss is reported honestly, not concealed.

SCENARIO-GROUPING GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOW SHARED (per the Task-9.0/9.3-review findings, restated here per the task brief) -- `_fig7_target_subset` (built on the newly-generalized `_scenario_target_subset`, also used by `_fig5_target_subset`) filters `targets/fig7.json`'s observable lists to ONLY the requested fraction's `initial_infection_fraction`-tagged entries before any band comparison, and raises `ValueError` (never silently falls back to the unfiltered, multi-scenario list) if a fraction has zero matching entries for any observable; verified in pytest for BOTH the filter and the raise (`test_fig7_target_subset_scenario_grouping_guard`), closing the Task-9.3-review-flagged gap that this pattern was previously checked only interactively -- see task-9.4-report.md.
